art.subject: Pomarine Jaeger (Stercorarius pomarinus), adult pale morph in breeding plumage, as seen off Korean coasts during spring passage in April-May: blackish-brown cap extending down below the gape over the face; cheeks and neck sides washed yellow; throat and belly white; a broad dark brown breast band, often mottled, and dark barring on the flanks; vent and undertail coverts dark brown; upperparts and wings uniform dark brown, with white shafts on the outer primaries forming a small white flash at the base of the primaries above and a larger white patch below; central tail feathers elongated into broad, blunt, twisted spoons; bill heavy, pale pinkish-grey on the basal two-thirds with a dark hooked tip; dark eye; black legs and feet.
art.pose: flying low over the sea in steady, gull-like flight, side view with the spoon-shaped tail projections visible
art.scene: open sea off the Korean coast in May, grey-blue waves under bright spring light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Large, heavy-bodied skua, about the size of a Black-tailed Gull but deeper-chested and pot-bellied, with broad-based pointed wings and a steady, gull-like flight. Bill stout, shorter than the head, with a strongly hooked tip. Legs short and black, with webbed feet. Tail wedge-shaped, with the central pair extended as broad, rounded, twisted plates that look like a thick club when seen from the side.
avoid: Do not paint long thin pointed tail streamers (Long-tailed Jaeger) or short pointed projections (Parasitic Jaeger); this species has broad, blunt, twisted spoons.
Do not paint a grey back and white body like a gull; the upperparts are uniformly dark brown.
Do not paint an all-black or yellow bill; it is pale with a dark hooked tip.
Do not paint a slender, tern-like body.
